concise_summary: PKD integrates biblical apocalyptic exegesis with philosophical metaphysics, arguing that reality operates through paradoxical inversion (fool-as-king, hidden court within apparent court) and heuristic problem-solving that pre-solves effects through retrograde consciousness. His culminating insight redefines Christ not as a historical person but as the zero-one binary event of pure novelty that invades mechanistic causality from outside, making universe-recreation continuous and teleological rather than determined.
key_claims: The Ancient of Days (Daniel 7) and Christ as eschatological judge (Revelation 1:13) are functions describing the same divine principle of judgment and sovereignty, suggesting Christ is archetypal rather than personified
Eleatic continuum metaphysics, not mechanistic cause-and-effect, explains purposeful reality shifts and justifies mystical experiences like the Tagore 'ensouling of animals' vision
The ostensible fool in Shakespeare's Hamlet is the true king and judge whose moral laws covertly obtain; reality is a ritualized pageant concealing inverted hierarchies
Heuristic problem-solving works backward from desired solutions through unconscious processes, meaning solutions pre-exist in consciousness before 'forward' reasoning; this is how creativity works
Christ must be redefined as the zero-one binary flip itself—pure novelty ex nihilo that cannot mechanistically follow from prior causes, continuously invading and recreating reality
Teilhard de Chardin's Point Omega falsely assumes spontaneous convergence; instead Christ/novelty requires ceaseless external intervention to prevent system decay
recurring_concepts: The Fool as Hidden King (inversion motif)
VALIS as incomplete conception (missing the void/zero)

uncertainty_flags: The identity of 'Narr' and 'Torr' in the fool-as-king passage is unclear; these may be abbreviations, proper names, or scribal shorthand not explained in the text
What precisely is 'Fledermaus' doing as an analogy? The connection between the opera's party scene and PKD's theological argument is asserted but not explained

The reference to PKD's 'Eleatic continuum view' is presented as his established framework, but the Eleatics (Parmenides, Zeno) are ancient Greek philosophers—the exact synthesis PKD claims is not elaborated
When did the Tagore vision occur? It is referenced as established fact but no date or full description is provided
The April 1981 entries (points 4-5) are dated 2.5 years after the October 1978 entries—has PKD revised his Christ theology significantly, or are these developments of the same insight?
PKD's claim that the 0-1 flicker happens 'every trillionth of a second' is presented as direct insight, not sourced to any physics or computer science text
The relationship between Hartshorne's pantheism and PKD's binary system is stated but not fully developed—are they compatible or is PKD modifying process theology?

It consists of (1) developing a conception of what one expects to discover, (2) using that conception to guide one in seeking, selecting, and assigning meaning to facts, and (3) continually developing new, more adequate conceptions as the discovery and interpretation of facts proceeds. Advocates of the procedure contend that all scientific knowledge is acquired in this manner and that all knowledge is relative, tentative, dubitable, and ever subject to change, there being no end to the heuristic process." COMMENT: This is a negative feedback loop familiar in electronic circuitry; the output signal is fed back into the input signal and modifies it, with the result that a very rapid series of self-controlling, self-regulating (that is, homeostatic) corrections is set up that amounts to high-velocity reprogramming. As the solution improves as output, it being backfed into the circuit's input, the self-correction occurs so fast that for all intents and purposes there is an ex nihilo problem-solving taking place in which that (solution) which is to be found (as the goal of the process) exists at the start of the process. "(They) pointed out the indispensibility in creative human thinking, as in its computer simulations, of what they call 'heuristics.' A large number of possibilities may have to be examined, but the search is organized heuristically in such a way that the directions most likely to lead to success are explored first. Means of ensuring that a solution will occur within a reasonable time, certainly much faster than by random hunting, include adoption of successive subgoals and working backward from the final goal (the formula to be proved, the state of affairs to be brought about)." COMMENT: "...working backward from the final goal." In other words, retrograde reasoning. For every conscious line of thought (problem-solving) that goes in the normal direction (from cause to effect) there is an obscured, provisional effect-to-cause retrograde line of thought, or in fact many of them, with each abolished as soon as the goal is better formulated; thus only the ultimate goal reaches consciousness; that is, the final goal arrived at. By its nature, then, heuristic problem-solving procedure in human minds will consist of mainly unconscious or subliminal processes lying outside the awareness of the person. All he will know is that somehow as if ex nihilo that which is to be proved or found is there in his mind as premise; there for input, not solution. This means that the heuristic processes have already occurred, and what reasoning he now employs is ex post facto; the problem has already been solved. folder 84 - 005 folder 84 - 005 April 20, 1981. PAY OFF: The introjection of Christ into the system is certainly the epitome of the adding of ex nihilo newness, of revitalizing creation as if from outside. Thus the term "Christ" _has_ to refer to any and all newness choices wherever and whenever they occur; "Christ" is the zero - one binary disjunctive event per se, and so is always now and always here. We see it and understand that we see (and experience) Christ, and this is newness, re-creation (in an unending process of creation). Christ _never_ arises/occurs as a result of the past, as an effect of antecedent causes; he is always born "from outside." Hence his epiphany can never be induced or predicted (by definition). Christ is that which does not follow mechanically: he always _invades_ world. To see, then, that Causality is not observed --that the "effect" is in fact not an effect at all --of its cause-- but is ex nihilo new is to see --literally, not symbolically-- Christ. Hence where there is Christ it is always the case that there has been "a perturbation of the reality field," something acting on it, intruding on it, invading it, "from outside." In terms of mechanical cause-and-effect Christ can never be said to be a _normal_ event derived from the antecedent system. Without these periodic insertions the system would run down; it would loss [sic] shape, organization and vitality. Cause-and-effect, then, taken in itself, is a losing game. The only thing that Christ can be said to be a result of --Christ as an event in the reality field-- _is the need of this event._ It is physically, mechanically causeless; it is absolutely teleological. Efficient causation has no bearing on it and will never yield it up (here Pierre Teilhard de Chardin is totally wrong; world is not spontaneously converging into the point omega; what he calls "Point Omega" is something done ceaselessly to world, an endless invasion). Wherever the effect is correctly seen to exceed its cause (which is then by definition not its cause) there is Christ. Conversely, wherever effect follows cause actually, there he is not. Christ, then, is an event, something that occurs in and to the reality field; Christ is not a person as men are persons.
